newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mostly up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates mostly up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday supported by the active A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 13.80 percent from 13.15 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 6.1 million lots from 9.0 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the active A share market was the major positive factor supporting the short term contracts.
"Some institutions were seen borrowing heavily from the market to speculate on the brisk A share market," said one trader.
"There will be a number of new issues in the next week, boosting fund demand on the early-maturing contracts," said another trader.
Traders said the rates were likely to rise further as a result of the new issues in the next few days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Wednesday with most investors turning their attention to the bullish A share markets, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell slightly to 120.08 yuan from 120.16 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose to 938,418 lots from 725,271 lots.
"Many investors are attracted by the A share markets which they believe to be more profitable," said one trader.
